solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pull this to swing the lead

definitions.text: Pull this to swing the lead

parts.note: the phrase 'pull a ...' is the idiom for faking a day off work
British idiom for shirking work by pretending to be ill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' and 'lead' suggest a dog on a leash, but swinging the lead is British slang for skiving; a sickie is a day off work claimed falsely as sick leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a bogus sick day is the classic way to shirk, so the informal word for that day fits.

clue.text: Most robust porter is in Gard du Nord

parts.note: porter and stout are both dark beers
est is the French for is, fitting a Paris railway station

explanation.surface: The strongest beer is served at the Paris railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a station porter at the Gare du Nord, but it is the beer; French 'est' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective means sturdy and strong, so its superlative means most robust.

clue.text: Outline opportunity to meet inmates?

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prison inmate
a tour is a visit around a place, a chance to meet those inside

explanation.surface: A prison visit arranged so outsiders can meet the inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer becomes a tour of the cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is the outline of a shape, such as a line on a map joining equal heights.

clue.text: Tiny bits of 10 on unfinished job

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the digits 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O

indicators.note: the job word loses its final letter

parts.note: a task

explanation.surface: Small fragments of something left when a job was abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference but reads as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is the smallest Greek letter, hence a very small amount; plural for tiny bits.

clue.text: Fake news: $1000 invested by island player

indicators.note: invested means clothed or wrapped in, so the thousand sits inside the island word

parts.note: an ait (or eyot) is a small river island
a grand, abbreviated G
a prop is a forward position in rugby

explanation.surface: A disinformation story about an islander handed a thousand dollars to play some part.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT is a small island in a river, especially the Thames; a prop is a rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, so slanted fake news is a fair modern gloss.

clue.text: Chart evil con in action book with pictures

parts.note: a graph is a chart of data

indicators.note: the letters of evil con are set moving into a new order

parts.note: these two words are the raw letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Plotting a villain's scam in an illustrated thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chart' supplies the opening directly; only 'evil con' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic novel tells a full-length story in comic-strip illustrations.

clue.text: Idiot cheers inside castle in retaliation

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: the thanks word is placed within the castle word

parts.note: a fort
ta, British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A fool raising a toast inside a castle provokes a reprisal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit is British slang for a fool, and ta is British informal thanks, like cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means a blow returned for a blow, i.e. retaliation in kind.

clue.text: Gentleman served up possibly a German dish

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: sir, the form of address for a gentleman
Otto is a typical German first name

explanation.surface: A gentleman, perhaps German, being served a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' suggests a waiter, but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: One of seven old harps played

indicators.note: the instruments being played suggests the letters being rearranged

parts.note: O, abbreviation for old
the word is used as written, its letters joining the O for rearranging

explanation.surface: One of seven ancient harps is plucked.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven are the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharos lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: Fancy mineral coating twisted bronze

indicators.note: the mineral word wraps around the other piece as a coat would

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock

indicators.note: twisted here means turned round, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: tan, the colour of a suntan

explanation.surface: Someone admiring an elaborate mineral specimen encrusted on a twisted bronze sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bronze' looks like the metal, but it is the colour of a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborately decorated, which is what ornate describes.

clue.text: Drinks one in front of adult film

indicators.note: the numeral piece comes before the adult letter in the answer

parts.note: Fanta is a fizzy soft drink brand, made plural
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Buying drinks before an adults-only film.
explanation.walkthrough: The brand name Fanta supplies the opening; 'adult film' tempts towards something racier.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated feature set to classical music.

clue.text: Relatives perhaps written as 'Ca' and 'Ab'

parts.note: siblings sharing only one parent
Cain and Abel each cut in two, leaving half of each brother's name

explanation.walkthrough: Ca and Ab look like chemical symbols, but they are the first halves of Cain and Abel, the Bible's first brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Siblings sharing only one parent are called this, and each name here is literally cut in half.

clue.text: TIME regularly parodies every PM

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of parodies is kept

parts.note: its second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are the ones kept
each, as in every one

explanation.surface: A magazine sneering that it mocks every prime minister without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals in TIME suggest the magazine, but it is just the time abbreviation. Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'parodies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the head of the Irish government, Ireland's prime minister.

clue.text: Excel not in DOS: ultimately scrapped

parts.note: out is the opposite of in

indicators.note: the last letter of DOS is thrown away

parts.note: the old Microsoft operating system name, taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that Microsoft Excel never ran under DOS and was dropped in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel' and 'DOS' both look like software, but Excel is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass others, which is what outdoing them means.

clue.text: Layering stone meets with approval

parts.note: ST, the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
ratification is formal approval of a treaty or agreement

explanation.surface: A paving stone design is signed off by the planners.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratification is arrangement in strata, the geological term for layers of rock.

clue.text: Pour wine around base of very cold dessert

parts.note: to tip is to pour out

indicators.note: the rice wine surrounds the next two letters

parts.note: sake, Japanese rice wine

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so the last letter

parts.note: the word is taken as written and only its bottom letter is used

explanation.surface: Pouring wine over a very cold pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Sake is Japanese rice wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipsy cake is a British pudding of sponge soaked in wine or sherry, like a trifle.

clue.text: PS maybe Dad & Ned in trouble, not sure

indicators.note: being in a mess suggests the letters of the two names are jumbled

parts.note: the name is taken as written for rearranging
the name is taken as written for rearranging
um, the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A postscript worrying that Dad and Ned may be in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is an example of an addendum, something added at the end of a document.

clue.text: Reliable officer roared across epicentre of battle

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

indicators.note: the roaring word spans across the middle letters, holding them inside

parts.note: boomed, as a loud voice or cannon does

indicators.note: the epicentre is the very centre, so the two middle letters of battle

parts.note: a six-letter word whose two central letters are the doubled consonant

explanation.surface: A police officer bellowing across the heart of a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle' has six letters, so its centre is the double T.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottomed means thoroughly dependable, from ships sheathed in copper below the waterline.

clue.text: Illuminant cat almost overturned, 50A reportedly

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned means turned upside down, read backwards
the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lion, a big cat
50 is the Roman numeral L and A the symbol for amp; spoken aloud, L amp is the lighting word

explanation.surface: A cat nearly knocks over a fifty-amp light fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: '50A' looks like a cross-reference but is L (Roman 50) plus A for amp.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil lamp gives light by burning oil through a wick, so it is a source of illumination.

clue.text: Release overseen by second high-up lawman?

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is watched from above by the first

parts.note: mo, a moment
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A prisoner's release supervised by a senior officer of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-up' sounds like rank, but a Mountie rides a horse, so sits high up.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police patrols on horseback, raised above the ground.

clue.text: Forged pieces?

indicators.note: forged means hammered into new shape, so the letters of pieces are reworked

parts.note: the word as written supplies the letters to be reshaped

explanation.surface: Counterfeit coins, with the question mark hinting at another sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Forged looks like counterfeit, but coins are honestly forged at a mint too.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in coin form, metal pieces struck at a mint.

clue.text: Cloud Yankee is in

definitions.note: an adjective: being in with someone means on friendly terms

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud of smoke or gloom
Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A weather report: an American is caught under a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the definition, as in being in with the right crowd; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in with someone means friendly and well liked, which is what pally conveys informally.

clue.text: 3 overlooking hard family's elevated dwelling

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the hard letter is left out of the number

parts.note: the number written as a word
a house is a dynasty, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Three houses on a hill look down on a tough family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' suggests a view from above, but it means missing out: three without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A treehouse is a playhouse built up among the branches, literally a raised home.

clue.text: Courage of rector interrupting Passion

indicators.note: the clergy letter breaks into the middle of the passion word

parts.note: heat means strong passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A vicar shows courage by interrupting a Passion play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion' suggests Easter, but it is heat, as in the heat of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or spirit, as in losing heart or taking heart.

clue.text: Artist in country skinned best game

indicators.note: the artist sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Chad, the African country
RA, a Royal Academician

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters of best are peeled off

parts.note: the word is taken as written, then its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A painter abroad gets cruelly beaten by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Academician gives RA, the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is the party game of miming words for teammates to guess.

clue.text: Male insect? Setter had another sort

definitions.note: refers back to the insect just named: a mantid is another kind of insect

parts.note: an ant
the setter says I had, shortened to I'D

explanation.surface: A setter admits that, when asked for a male insect, he had another kind in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's own word 'insect': the answer is a different sort of insect from the ant in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantid is a praying mantis, a separate kind of insect from the ant.

clue.text: European really embraces iron drink

indicators.note: the word for really wraps itself around the ironing word

parts.note: so, as in 'I so want to'
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A continental traveller insists his drink is fortified with iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' is the verb, as in ironing a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee forced through ground beans, a short drink.

clue.text: Course bamboozled Master

indicators.note: bamboozled means confused, so the letters of master are mixed up

parts.note: the word is taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster confounded by his own course.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream follows a course; as a noun course also means a flowing watercourse.
